text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: p99 spike detected for customer XenonCorp (tenant: xenon-42) in eu1 dedicated pool dp-eu1. Current window: p95=210ms, p99=2.8s (SLO target p99 <= 500ms). Auto-notify: infra-oncall.

miguel: grabbing. seeing sustained p99 ~2.5-3s across multiple hosts in dp-eu1. dash shows request qps for xenon-42 up ~6x last 30m.

anya: confirm whether this is tail latency on generation or embeddings?

carl: logs show a lot of long-sequence generate calls from xenon-42: typical seq_len 8k-45k, some multipart uploads. Might be batch bulk-ingest jobs they started.

amanda: Xenon account says they kicked off a large ad-hoc migration at 09:15 UTC, moving historical customer messages into our embed pipeline. They just replied to our webhook saying it's a bulk run.

miguel: okay, priority is to protect SLO for other tenants and reduce impact on Xenon UX. Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) throttle xenon-42 to soft-QPS cap 2) isolate heavy requests to a quarantined slot 3) scale dp-eu1 by +2 replicas temporary 4) failover some traffic to hosted fallback models if needed.

kevin: I can patch routing policy to limit xenon-42 to 30 rps on dp-eu1. doing now: `redwoodctl routing update-policy --pool dp-eu1 --tenant xenon-42 --rate-limit 30`

jen: heads-up — scaling dp-eu1 may take ~4-6 mins for new GPU workers to register. If the tail is due to KV cache misses and larger KV footprint, scaling might not help immediate p99.

anya: good point. any evidence of KV cache pressure?

carl: yes, GPU mem pressure and KV evictions spike correlated with the bulk ingest. Logs: `kv_cache_evictions: 1200/min` and `gpu_mem_pressure > 92%` on host dp-eu1-07 and dp-eu1-09.

miguel: start tenant isolation to dedicated quarantine pool to keep other tenants safe. Command: ```
redwoodctl isolate-tenant --from-pool dp-eu1 --to-pool quarantine-eu1 --tenant xenon-42 --mode draining
```

kevin: applied transient routing. Traffic for xenon-42 now draining to quarantine-eu1 for new requests. Older in-flight requests continue on dp-eu1.

amanda: notifying Xenon support now that we've throttled and started isolation. message: "We've limited your concurrent jobs to reduce impact on other customers. Contact us if you need a dedicated ingest window."

incident-bot: deploy-bot: scaled pool dp-eu1 +2 replicas (requested by kevin). new replicas registering: dp-eu1-13, dp-eu1-14.

jen: checking metrics after isolate+throttle: p99 for other tenants in dp-eu1 back to 420ms. overall cluster p99 trending down.

carl: quarantine pool still experiencing high p99 for xenon-42 (p99 ~2.3s) — likely their long sequences still cost tokens per-request. Recommend enabling chunked processing on their pipeline or a job-scheduler for large batches to avoid single huge generation calls.

anya: Ops question: can we apply per-request sequence-length cap at the ingress to enforce an upper bound? Something like `max_tokens=4096` fallback to an async job if over-limit.

miguel: we have an API layer knob. propose this immediate policy: if seq_len > 12k, return 429 with guidance for async bulk endpoint. Command: ```
redwoodctl policy set --tenant xenon-42 --pool quarantine-eu1 --rule "max_seq_len:12000 -> status:429; route:bulk-ingest"
```

kevin: policy pushed. We'll also surface a client-friendly message to Xenon SDK docs link to async ingestion patterns.

amanda: Xenon replies: they can re-run with chunked mode but asked for temporary higher throughput for a 2-hour window; they're requesting exception.

miguel: Given risk to SLOs for other customers, we deny an unbounded exception. Offer a scheduled dedicated maintenance window with reserved capacity (Dedicated burst) — ops can provision dedicated nodes for them if they commit.

amanda: I've proposed 2 extra dedicated nodes for 2 hours as paid burst; Xenon accepted. I issued an order to provisioning: `billing.reserve-burst xenon-42 --pool dp-eu1 --nodes 2 --duration 120m`

incident-bot: billing-bot: burst reservation created, provisioning in progress.

jen: provisioning finished. spun up nodes dp-eu1-burst-1/2 and attached to tenant-only routing. Moving xenon workload to burst nodes now.

carl: after moving to burst nodes, xenon p99 dropped to 560ms — still slightly above SLO but way better. Remaining tail is due to a few requests still hitting long retrieval latency from their pre-processing.

anya: ask Xenon to enable chunking and reduce per-request token counts; give step-by-step. Amanda to track. Also set follow-up: create Eval to measure tails under chunking.

amanda: noted. I'll send the SDK snippets: ```
// JS: chunked client pseudocode
for (const chunk of chunkify(inputs, {maxTokens:8000})) {
  await client.generate({model: 'x-embed', input: chunk});
}
```

miguel: oncall summary for handoff to next shift: - incident start 2923456789, root cause: bulk long-sequence jobs from Xenon tenant causing KV cache pressure and GPU mem high - actions taken: throttled tenant, isolated to quarantine pool, scaled +2, created paid burst nodes, moved traffic - customer impact: Xenon user p99 degraded to ~2.8s for ~35m, other tenants SLOs protected after isolation - next steps: require Xenon to switch to chunked ingestion, add per-tenant async ingestion option, add alert for large seq_len spikes.

kevin: tagging this thread with `#postmortem-needed` and raising a ticket in PM board: `PM-RED-1428` for design of async ingest and per-tenant quotas.

amanda: Xenon accepted scheduled maintenance and will not run further bulk jobs until chunking tested. They asked for a quick retro call 09:45 UTC. I've scheduled.

miguel: handing to anya for follow-up and long-term mitigation. I'm dropping from channel. Thanks everyone. :wave:

anya: taking over. I'll coordinate postmortem and action items. Adding notes: adjust alert threshold: when single-tenant qps > 4x baseline AND p99 > 1s => auto-isolate.

jen: leaving a small runbook snippet for future on-call: ```
1) Check dashboards for KV evictions and gpu_mem_pressure
2) If single tenant causing spike: throttle -> isolate -> scale -> offer burst -> request client chunking
3) Notify CS and offer paid burst or scheduled window
4) Create follow-up PM ticket for async ingestion
```

miguel: ack. handing off. last check: overall dp-eu1 p99 across tenants stable at 380ms. closing active mitigation.

incident-bot: incident resolved flag set by miguel. severity: customer-impact (Xenon), duration ~70m.

amanda: will follow up with Xenon and close external comms after retro.

anya: thanks team. adding labels: `tenant-isolation`, `dedicated-burst`, `postmortem-pending`.

jen: good job all.
